standard_prerequisites: The cycle class of an integral closed subspace as the class of its structure sheaf, and the compatibility of flat pullback and proper pushforward with the cycle classes attached to coherent sheaves
Stability of properness and of flatness of a given relative dimension under base change
Flat base change in cohomology for a proper morphism, identifying the pushforward of the pulled back structure sheaf with the pullback of the pushforward
core_obligations: Record that the base changed morphism is again proper and that the projection is again flat of the same relative dimension, so both sides of the identity make sense
Reduce the identity of cycles to the case of the class of a single integral closed subspace, using that cycle classes are additive

Rewrite that class as the cycle class of the structure sheaf of the subspace, and use the compatibility of pullback and pushforward with cycle classes of coherent sheaves to reduce the identity to an isomorphism of two coherent modules
Obtain that isomorphism from flat base change in cohomology for the proper morphism, which finishes the proof
proof_roadmap: Check properness and flatness of the base changed morphisms
Reduce to the class of one integral closed subspace and to its structure sheaf
Apply the compatibility with cycle classes and flat base change in cohomology
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the base change compatibility of flat pullback with proper pushforward at the lemma labelled lemma-flat-pullback-proper-pushforward (label line 1498), whose own proof immediately follows the statement. The proof first records that the base changed morphism stays proper and that the projection stays flat of the same relative dimension, then reduces a general cycle to the class of a single integral closed subspace and rewrites that class as the class of the structure sheaf of the subspace. Through the compatibility of pullback and pushforward with cycle classes of coherent sheaves the cycle identity becomes an isomorphism of two coherent modules, which is supplied by flat base change in cohomology for the proper morphism. The counted statement records neither the reduction to a closed subspace nor the cohomological input.
